All right, the recent changes are looking solid. I added the `unfinished_work_remains` helper, rewrote the rate‑limit handoff check to call it, and introduced corresponding tests that verify its behavior both when the tasks file is missing and when it contains unchecked boxes. The linting and test suite now report 26 passing tests, so the codebase is healthy.

Now I need to make sure the documentation stays in sync with the updated logic. The `docs/functions.md` file contains the description for `rate_limit_handoff`. I recall that the current wording says:

> “Afterwards sleeps whatever remains of the window (skipped when all tasks are already done) and returns so the loop switches back to opencode (the faster of the two).”

But after the refactor, the condition for skipping the sleep has changed. Previously, the code would skip the remaining sleep if **all tasks were already done**, which implicitly meant that `tasks.md` existed and had zero unchecked tasks. The new implementation uses `unfinished_work_remains()`, which returns `True` when the tasks file is missing (i.e., we assume there is unfinished work) and only returns `False` when the file exists *and* there are zero unchecked tasks. Consequently, the sleep is now skipped **only** when `tasks.md` exists and contains no unchecked tasks. If the file doesn’t exist yet (e.g., during the initial planning phase), the function returns `True`, and the sleep proceeds as before, ensuring that the rate‑limit window is respected even before any tasks have been written.

The docs need to reflect this nuance so that future readers understand the exact behavior. I should locate the exact sentence in `functions.md` and replace it with a more precise description. I’ll use the Edit tool with `replace_all: false` to target just this line. The old string will be the exact phrase as it appears, and the new string will elaborate:

> “Afterwards sleeps whatever remains of the window (skipped only when ralph/tasks.md exists with zero unchecked tasks, per `unfinished_work_remains`; a planning‑phase limit with no tasks.md yet still sleeps so the plan retry waits out the window) and returns so the loop switches back to opencode (the faster of the two).”

That captures both the new skip condition and the intended behavior during the planning phase. I’ll now issue the edit command accordingly.
